title: jmap-search: generic filter-expression extension for every JMAP type
description:
Mark 2026-10-23. Goal: query every JMAP data type with one filter language, derived from the built-in language of draft-atwood-jmap-graph-search-00 (§where). Not before the 0.4 publish; all additive (every *FilterCondition is #[non_exhaustive]).

MINIMUM (do regardless of WG outcome): define a jmap-search extension with its own capability id for our own implementations (proposed urn:ietf:params:jmap:search; confirm naming with Mark), so our servers/clients can interoperate on it.

DESIGN:
1. New draft in ~/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec (e.g. draft-atwood-jmap-search-00): lift the graph-independent part of graph-search: field tests as JSON Pointers into the /get representation, comparison ops ($eq $ne $gt $gte $lt $lte $in $nin $exists $prefix $contains), array rules, logical ops ($and $or $not), $collation (default code-point), $text (server-defined, like Email text). Adds a 'where' property to the FilterCondition of each /query whose type is listed in the capability's dataTypes (same per-type listing pattern as metadata-04). No new result formats; paging, sort, /queryChanges, result references unchanged.
2. Generic /query for types that lack one: for each listed type without a /query (Calendar, TaskList, ParticipantIdentity, Identity, ...), define a standard Foo/query (and /queryChanges) whose filter supports only 'where'. This subsumes the original Calendar/TaskList/ParticipantIdentity /query idea.
3. Rebase graph-search onto it: generic language plus the structural operators $edge $reachable $from $to.
4. Metadata: pointers such as /metadata/<ns>/<key> give metadata filtering; note the relationship to the six metadata-04 filter conditions.
5. Server cost: let servers refuse unindexed paths (unsupportedFilter / queryTooComplex) and/or advertise which pointers per type they index. Keep the access-control rule: only what /get would show.

CODE: move the type-neutral core of jmap-graph-types search.rs (Expression::parse etc.) and the evaluator in jmap-graph-server search.rs into a shared crate; graph keeps the structural part. Wire 'where' into the MemoryBackends (they store JSON, so pointer evaluation is cheap), mail first.

WG: sound out jmap@ietf.org before a full draft (RFC 8620 deliberately uses per-type filters; reception unknown). Frame as a new optional extension, not a calendars gap (see FINDING note: calendars -30 deliberately removed the stray Calendar/query mention). Every upstream write (list post, issue, PR) needs Mark's explicit go.
notes: FINDING 2026-10-23: checked every draft-ietf-jmap-calendars revision -00..-33. 'Calendar/query' appears exactly once in -01 through -29, always in the same mayReadFreeBusy sentence ('MUST NOT be returned in Calendar/get and Calendar/query'); no revision ever had a Calendar/query section (-01 TOC: 3.1 get, 3.2 changes, 3.3 set). -00 lacks the sentence. In -30 the authors replaced it with 'MUST NOT be returned in "Calendar/get" or "Calendar/changes" responses', i.e. a deliberate editorial correction. So the WG question 'was the -26 mention intended?' is already answered (no); frame any proposal as a new feature (likely a separate extension), not a gap in calendars. Our CalendarFilterCondition {name, isSubscribed} was our own scaffolding from 537fac26 (2026-05-04), not from any draft.
